# rediscloud_iris_identity_api_key (Resource)

Manages a direct Iris identity resource, independently of Redis Cloud CAPI.

The sensitive `token` is returned only during creation and retained through
refresh and updates. Import cannot recover it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "rediscloud_iris_identity_api_key" "example" {
  name       = "application-runtime"
  expires_at = 0
  grants_json = jsonencode([{
    tenant       = "your-tenant"
    product      = "memory"
    resourceType = "store"
    resourceId   = rediscloud_iris_agent_memory.example.id
    actions      = ["read", "write"]
  }])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)

### Optional

- `expires_at` (Number) Unix seconds after which the key no longer authenticates; 0 or omitted means never.
- `grants_json` (String) JSON-encoded service configuration. Use jsonencode(...). Grants where an empty list is not a meaningful answer. On create and update, an
explicitly supplied but empty list is a caller mistake rather than a request to
clear grants. On API-key introspection, reporting an active key with no grants
would read to a data plane as an authenticated caller with no authorization, so
the response must either carry grants or fail.
- `user_id` (String) The user that the key acts as. Optional: a key without a user acts as no user. It cannot change after the mint. Requires API key user binding to be enabled in the deployment. The deployment admin and an on-prem suite_admin can set any user; another caller can set only its own user ID.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Number)
- `id` (String) Resource identifier used for import.
- `key_id` (String)
- `rotated_from` (String)
- `tenant_id` (String) Immutable tenant that owns this key, independently of its grants.
- `token` (String, Sensitive)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import rediscloud_iris_identity_api_key.example 33333333333333333333333333333333
```
